cohort: The study analyzed medical records of 852 singleton pregnancies from two consecutive years (2018 and 2019), comprising FGR, SGA, and control fetuses.
finding: Fetuses with FGR had higher cesarean section rates and worse perinatal outcomes compared to SGA and control fetuses.
mod_finding: Most FGR fetuses were delivered by cesarean section and allocated in Robson groups 5.2 to 10, while vaginal delivery occurred in nearly 60% of FGR fetuses allocated in Robson groups 1-5.1 without a significant increase in perinatal morbidity.
